newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Corimon share doubles on Caracas bolsa.
newsitem.headline: Corimon share doubles on Caracas bolsa.

text.p: Venezuelan paints and packaging company Corimon returned Monday to trading screens after an eight-month suspension on the Caracas bolsa, doubling its share price at the opening to 20.25 bolivars from Friday's 9.50 bolivar price.

"Basically the stock is catching up with the rest of the market's rise," said Banesco broker Simon Brad. The Caracas bolsa's index is up nearly 100 percent in dollar terms since the start of the year.
"But it's very speculative; some investors don't want to know, others think it a good play. It will take time to level out," he added.
At 0955 EST, the stock stood at 16.25 bolivars.
Financially-troubled Corimon, once Venezuela's industrial conglomerate par excellence, was suspended from the Caracas and New York Stock exchanges in February.
It has since restructured over $100 million in debt, re- focused operations and sold off foreign subsidiaries.
The company reported a third quarter net profit of 700 billion bolivars last Friday, down from 1.782 billion bolivars in the same quarter of 1995.
Venezuela's National Securities Commission (CNV) removed the company's Caracas bolsa trading suspension on Friday. The company has also filed to resume trade on the New York Stock Exchange.
The suspension was removed "because there was no longer any obstacle, the conditions are there for it to return to the market," a CNV spokeswoman said last week.
